provisions.text: Coach/economy for domestic and international; premium economy/business need written pre-approval by president/VP/dean attached; OCONUS segments > 5 h and CONUS segments > 5 h allow premium economy/business for faculty and staff
Accommodation other than coach for a medical condition goes through EEO/ER; no medical information on the report
provisions.why_not: an EEO letter is an HR document, never in a receipt folder

provisions.text: Federally funded travel must be booked as economy airfare
Lowest available airfare: direct route, at most two connections, no extra stays, standard bags, usually a restricted coach fare
Tickets bought with frequent-flyer miles are not reimbursed; miles may be used to upgrade if the fare paid is the lowest; the cost of a paid upgrade is the traveler's
Out-of-pocket tickets bought through iBuy+ Travel / Travel Leaders can be claimed within 60 days of purchase regardless of travel dates
Airfare on a US government grant must be on a US carrier (Fly America / Open Skies)
Standard checked bags, in-flight Wi-Fi and advance seat assignment within economy are paid
Priority boarding, exit row, extra legroom, Economy Plus, window/aisle seat fees are not paid unless pre-approved (premium economy for segments > 5 h)
Passport, visa, Global Entry and TSA PreCheck fees for employees who travel routinely, subject to departmental approval
Indirect or interrupted routes are paid at the lower of the actual fare and the direct-route fare, documented with a screenshot at booking
Change/cancellation penalties are allowable when documented with a business reason
Unused tickets and credits belong to the university; refunds must be requested
Charter aircraft need prior written approval of the President/EVP/CFO/Provost and Risk Management
provisions.why_not: an executive approval process, not a receipt

provisions.text: Airline club membership fees are unallowable

provisions.page: App. A p.28, App. B p.30
provisions.text: Baggage of a personal nature (golf clubs, skis, bicycles, surfboards) is unallowable
First class is unallowable except as an EEO medical accommodation

A business meal has two or more persons, business discussed; each attendee's name and the business purpose go on the line; group functions need the announcement or invitation list; attendees may not be an approver of the report
Travel meals are ordinary meals away from home on GW business, at actual cost
Per diem is used only for international travel (State Department rates built into Concur); per diem days need no receipts

The international meal per diem is claimed through Concur's Travel Allowance itinerary (the State Department rates are built in, pre-populated by the system); meals a host or a conference provided are marked there
Alcohol is separated from the meal and charged to 52611 – Entertainment; never to a federal grant
Alcohol and entertainment that cannot be charged to a sponsored award go to an unrestricted account
Supporting documents are required for every expense over $75; itemised receipts for meals over $75, including meals on a hotel bill
Level 3 / rich card data counts as a receipt for goods only when items are listed and the total matches; never for airfare, hotel, rental car or train
The Missing Receipt Affidavit (in Concur) or the Acknowledgement form replaces an itemised meal receipt; missing receipts are never accepted for airfare, hotel, trains or cars
A standard room, cost kept to a minimum; conference block rates booked directly are fine
Peer-to-peer lodging (Airbnb): faculty/staff strongly discouraged; students prohibited without prior written approval of the advisor's office and Risk Management
Deposits should be on a P-Card; deposit receipts list room nights and the rate per night; a group deposit needs the traveler names
Booking a hotel for a visitor: the hotel is paid in full in advance only when the rate requires prepayment; card numbers are never e-mailed
provisions.why_not: arranging a guest's booking is not a traveler's reimbursement

provisions.text: Prepaid bargain rates are risky: non-refundable and unchangeable
The folio is itemised by night (room rate + tax per night); personal charges on the folio are left out
Hotel cancellation / no-show penalties from failing to cancel a guaranteed reservation are unallowable

provisions.page: App. A p.28, App. B p.30
provisions.text: Laundry/dry cleaning only on trips longer than five calendar days
Non-business days added for personal reasons are not paid unless the stay-over lowers the total cost, with documentation

Over 200 miles commercial air is generally most economical; 200 miles or less by bus, shuttle, ride service, taxi, rental or private car; more than 200 miles by car needs a quote showing it was most economical
Most economical means to and from the airport; a second party driving the traveler is paid at the mileage rate but not more than a taxi or shuttle would cost
Hertz, Enterprise and National are preferred (insurance included at no extra charge); other companies: staff MUST buy CDW and liability coverage; students must rent from the preferred companies
Decline prepaid fuel and refuel before returning; gasoline for a rental is allowable
International rentals: staff must buy CDW and liability; students are not authorised to rent abroad
Up to full-size; specialty vehicles (luxury, SUV, convertible) are not reimbursed without prior written VP/dean approval; the traveler pays the daily excess
Students: authorised-driver program, 20+, licensed, no 15-passenger vans, not for personal use
Accidents are reported to the agency, Risk Management and the police
provisions.why_not: an incident report, not an expense

provisions.text: Private car: mileage at the IRS rate from the normal place of business (not the residence), plus tolls and reasonable parking; commuting is never paid; Concur has a mileage calculator
Two or more people in one car: mileage is paid to one person only
Rail and bus at the lowest fare with reserved seating when less expensive than air; evidence of the airfare comparison attached; Acela Business Class is allowable when more economical
A car in lieu of air is paid per mileage/rental rules but never more than the lowest available airfare, documented within two business days of approval
Private car services need the Vice President's written pre-approval attached; limos and cabs for extended distances are unallowable
Charter buses go through Travel Services with contract review
Fines, tickets, car repairs and car washes are unallowable
Gasoline for a personal vehicle is unallowable (mileage covers it)
Miscellaneous expenses over $75 per transaction must be documented
Travel advances $200–$2,500, reconciled within 30 days, unused repaid within 60 days
provisions.why_not: an advance is reconciled against the report, not filed from a receipt

provisions.text: Cakes, flowers, balloons for employee celebrations are not business expenses; decorations for university events are; gifts for an individual need prior written VP/dean approval attached
Entertainment must advance a university business relationship, within good taste and reasonable limits
Submit within 30 days after the trip; out-of-pocket claims older than 60 days after the trip are not reimbursed; students are exempt from the 60-day limit
Out-of-pocket travel cannot be claimed before the trip unless booked through iBuy+ Travel
One report per trip; several one-line reports are discouraged
The business purpose says what, who, why and the benefit to GW; 'Attend conference' is inadequate
'Is this a vendor invoice?' is yes only for a true invoice; expenses paid to service providers go through P-Card / invoice processing, and payments to individuals through Payables
Nobody approves their own expenses; sponsored expenses route to OVPR
A GW employee acting as delegate submits a student's report
provisions.why_not: who submits is a Concur role, not a receipt

provisions.text: Local travel is under 50 miles one way: no personal meals or lodging — unless the mealtime falls within the hours of the meeting
Spouse/companion expenses only with VP pre-approval attached
Expenses paid or reimbursed by an outside source are unallowable
Foreign receipts are recorded in the receipt's currency; Concur converts; never convert by hand
The GW P-Card is the preferred payment method; P-Card charges are reconciled in Concur as card transactions, not as out-of-pocket lines
Room service, luggage storage fees, valet parking are allowable
Telephone, fax, internet and data costs are allowable but may not be charged to a federal research project

provisions.page: App. A p.29, App. B p.30
provisions.text: Tips are allowable when customary and not excessive; excessive tipping is not
Vaccinations and other medical costs when required for travel to specific destinations
Non-employee travel (applicants, guest lecturers, consultants) paid by GW on a P-Card
provisions.why_not: paid by GW, not reimbursed to the traveler

provisions.text: Clothing, shoes, jewelry, toiletries, medicines, in-room movies and alcohol, health club, babysitting, recreation, hairdressers, haircuts, personal care
Credit-card fees, annual membership, interest and late charges on personal cards
Life, accident, baggage, personal property or flight-interruption insurance premiums
Luggage or briefcase purchase or repair
Lost, broken or stolen property
Newspapers, magazines, books for personal use
Charitable contributions go through University Payables
Dependent care, pet care, home or lawn maintenance, other personal costs
Golf/tennis/health/country club fees, memberships and sporting equipment unless part of a pre-authorised group event
Penalties and fees for violating airline, rail, hotel or reservation rules
Flowers, fruit, candy, balloons for specific individuals unless approved in advance by a VP or dean, with the approval attached
The manual applies to all expenses incurred for a university purpose regardless of the account charged: a non-travel business expense is judged by the same manual

provisions.page: owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 4); Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.7–8
provisions.text: Subscriptions, office supplies, cloud services and membership dues paid out of pocket ARE reimbursable: file the line, with a notice that GW's preferred channel is P-Card / iBuy+ and that out-of-pocket reimbursement is to be confirmed by the department (GW's order of purchasing methods does not list self-payment, and no GW page allows or forbids it)

Mixed reports are allowed: a non-travel receipt found in a trip folder is filed ON that report with its dedicated expense type, plus a notice that it is a non-travel expense on a travel report (GW: a mix of Domestic and No Travel may pick either travel type)
A purely non-travel folder is one report whose header answers 'What type of travel expenses are you claiming?' with No Travel; no Travel Allowance itinerary

A document that is not reimbursed through a Concur expense report, or for which this account has no expense type, gets no line: the agent says 'not filed in Concur' and names the right channel (Concur Invoice non-employee reimbursement, University Payables / supplier invoice, payroll through the Provost's office, the Gift Card Order Form in Request, GW IT purchasing)

Out-of-pocket claims older than 60 days from the transaction date, or from the completion of travel, as applicable, are not reimbursed; a non-travel purchase counts from its transaction date (our reading of 'as applicable'); students and guests are exempt

GW's sales-tax exemption does not apply to purchases made with personal funds: the tax on a self-paid receipt is part of the expense (the new manual adds that P-Card holders are responsible for obtaining the exemption)

Subscriptions, computers, general office supplies, memberships and postage are administrative costs: charged directly to a federal award only when integral to the project, allocable to it, budgeted or approved by the sponsor, and not also recovered as indirect costs
Accepting click-through terms is signing a contract; faculty and staff have no authority to sign for the university without a written delegation
On sponsored funds a report with a type on the OVPR list (52221, 52193, 52441, 52691, 54541, 52641, 53131, 55151, 55541 …) routes to OVPR; 52211, 54111, 55567, 52199 and 52231 are not on the list
Only reading matter FOR PERSONAL USE is unallowable: a journal, database or news subscription for research or teaching is a business expense, type 52221-SUBSCRIPTIONS/PERIODICALS

What GW already provides at no cost — site-licensed software (MATLAB, Microsoft Office), the AAAS Elemental membership, the digital New York Times / Washington Post / Wall Street Journal — is filed when bought separately for business, with a needs_review flag asking why (no GW page forbids the purchase; the handling is our judgment)

GW names no expense type for software subscriptions and SaaS licences: where the kind is unclear, 52199, 55567, 52441 or 52221 is accepted, with a needs_review flag 'GW does not say which expense type software takes' (the portal calls 52199 'MFA USE ONLY'; the Controller lists it as the general non-capitalized software account). An item that clearly is one kind takes that type and needs no type flag: a usage-billed cloud bill is 55567 (NC-CLOUD-BILL), a journal, database or periodical subscription 52221 (NC-SUBS-BUSINESS)

provisions.page: https://procurement.gwu.edu/procurement-methods; Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.6–7; owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 6)
provisions.text: All software and SaaS purchases, regardless of dollar amount, must have a GW IT security assessment, and technology hardware, software or cloud services cannot be bought on a P-Card without one: a self-paid software, cloud or AI-tool line carries a needs_review flag saying so (GW IT's own page is narrower: restricted data, a connection to GW systems)

AI-tool subscriptions (ChatGPT, Claude) are reimbursable; they are not on GW IT's list of approved AI tools (Microsoft Copilot, Adobe Firefly, GW Chat, Box AI, Zoom AI, Google Gemini, NotebookLM), so the line carries a needs_review flag

provisions.page: Concur Add Expense dialog, read 2026-09-15 (55567 is in the Other section); https://it.gwu.edu/research-cloud; owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 6)
provisions.text: A cloud bill (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) paid personally is filed as 55567-CLOUD COMPUTING SERVICES, with the self-paid notice and the security-assessment flag; GW IT's Research Cloud offers researchers AWS resources

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.8; https://ibuy.gwu.edu/office-supplies-and-furniture; owner decision D-065 (2026-09-18)
provisions.text: Office supplies are 54111-OFFICE SUPPLIES (the main type only: 52691-MISCELLANEOUS OFFICE EXPENSE is not accepted for plain supplies — it takes an office cost that is not a supply, NC-OFFICE-NOT-SUPPLY). GW's preferred way to buy them is an iBuy+ punch-out supplier paid by P-Card; bought out of pocket they are filed with the self-paid notice
GW's Amazon Business account takes the P-Card only; an order on a PERSONAL Amazon account is an ordinary self-paid purchase (our reading): file it with the self-paid notice

A computer bought personally is filed under 52193-NON-CAPITALIZED COMPUTING EQUIPMENT when its unit price is under $5,000, with a needs_review flag: GW IT requires computers to be ordered through GW IT

Equipment or software with a unit price of $5,000 or more and a useful life over one year is capitalized (58524-CAPITALIZED COMPUTER EQUIPMENT AND SOFTWARE), which this account cannot select: not in Concur — GW IT purchasing

provisions.page: App. B p.30 (a partial listing, silent on professional dues); https://procurement.gwu.edu/appendix-procurement-competitive-exemptions-list (item 12); owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 4)
provisions.text: The manual has no clause on professional-society dues — App. B names only airline clubs, personal card fees and country, tennis, health or golf clubs. Dues of a professional society are 52211-MEMBERSHIPS, filed with the self-paid notice

Part-time Faculty Professional Development Fund: up to $100 of a professional organisation's membership is reimbursed (at most three awards and $1,400 per fiscal year), after the department's and the school's approval and the fund's own, claimed through Concur within 30 days of the activity; only part-time faculty eligible for good-faith consideration

provisions.page: owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 8); p.11–12 (new manual p.12); App. C p.32
provisions.text: A meal with a job candidate follows the business-meal rules — every attendee named, the purpose stated, alcohol split off to 52611; the type is 53102-US BUSINESS MEALS or 52641-RECRUITING EXPENSE

provisions.page: owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 8); App. A p.28 (new manual p.29)
provisions.text: App. A names non-employee travel (job applicants, guest lecturers, consultants) paid by GW on a P-Card. An employee who paid a candidate's hotel or airfare out of pocket files it — 53131-TRAVEL-NON-GWU PERSONNEL, the ordinary travel type or 52641 — with a needs_review flag
An employee's own trip to recruit or to interview is ordinary travel ('Travel to University of Washington to recruit students' is one of the manual's model purposes)

A job advertisement paid personally is filed under 55151-ADVERTISING or 52641 with a needs_review flag: fee-based postings are department funded, normally paid by P-Card or payment request and coordinated by Faculty Affairs or HR; advertising is generally unallowable on sponsored projects

A candidate's OWN out-of-pocket receipts are not an employee's expenses: a non-employee is reimbursed through Concur Invoice (invoice type 'Non-employee reimbursement': itemized receipts, a memo of the purpose, the payee's address) — not in Concur Expense
A search firm's invoice is an expense paid to a service provider: University Payables / supplier invoice — not in Concur Expense
A signing bonus is compensation, not an expense: payroll — not in Concur (that it runs through payroll is our inference; the page does not say how it is paid)

Inviting and paying foreign visitors: the visa type, the activity and the way of paying are settled with the Tax Department BEFORE the invitation; a payment made for a foreign candidate or visitor is filed with a needs_review flag

A new full-time faculty member's relocation is a lump sum from the Provost's office by rank — $3,000 assistant professor or instructor, $4,500 associate or full professor — paid through payroll and taxable, for any expense of the move including house-hunting trips; receipts only prove the move. Not a Concur expense report, and this account has no relocation type (53211-RELOCATION EXPENSE is not selectable)
Part-time faculty, and full-time faculty appointed for one semester, have no relocation allowance
Staff relocation: GW publishes no policy (the HR page lists only third-party moving discounts)
provisions.why_not: no GW rule to test against — the owner's decision is not to invent one

provisions.text: Table centerpieces, flowers and decorations for university events are allowable

provisions.page: owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 11); App. A p.28 (new manual p.29): 'alcohol must be charged to account 52611'
provisions.text: Gifts for an individual and decorations or flowers for a university event are 52612-SPECIAL EVENTS/BUSINESS RELATIONS (the portal asks for attendees on it); 52611-ENTERTAINMENT is alcohol and the entertainment of business contacts

provisions.page: https://ibuy.gwu.edu/expense-reporting-helpful-guidelines ('Purchase of Gift Cards', read 2026-09-18); owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 13)
provisions.text: Gift cards and cash equivalents need permission BEFORE the purchase: 'you must request permission to make the purchase via a Gift Card Order Form in iBuy+ under the Requests tab'. A card bought personally without it is not claimed on an expense report — not in Concur Expense (that it is then not filed at all is our reading: the page says nothing about claiming it afterwards)

A receipt that shows it was paid with the GW P-Card is FILED anyway — Payment Type can only be Out of Pocket, this account has no card feed — with a needs_review flag and the line Comment 'P-Card transaction; the card is not linked to this account; once it is linked, replace this line with the card transaction or delete it.' (the original AIR-PCARD-PAID and REG-PCARD follow it too since 2026-09-18, with lesson L-023 rewritten)

provisions.page: App. B p.31; owner decision D-019
provisions.text: A book for research or teaching is a business expense (only books for personal use are unallowable): type 52231-BOOKS

provisions.page: experience (the manual does not mention printing or copying); Concur Add Expense dialog
provisions.text: Printing, copying and binding by an outside shop: 55511-NON-GW PRINTING/REPRODUCTION, 52661-OFFICE COPYING - NOT GWU or 55513-BINDING

provisions.page: experience (the manual does not mention postage); https://compliance.gwu.edu/direct-charging-administrative-costs-associated-sponsored-projects
provisions.text: Postage and express mail for university business: 53411-POSTAGE/EXPRESS MAIL - NON-GW; an administrative cost on a federal award

provisions.page: App. A p.29; Concur Add Expense dialog; owner decision D-065 (2026-09-18)
provisions.text: Telephone, internet and data costs are allowable but never on a federal research project; outside a trip the type is 53311-TELEPHONE - DIRECT (the main type only: 53313-LONG DISTANCE USAGE is not accepted for a phone, hotspot or data plan)
Fees for attendance at seminars and conference registration are allowable: 53241-SEMINAR FEES or 53251-CONFERENCE/SEMINAR/TRAINING EXPENSE

provisions.page: experience; App. A p.28 (new manual p.29) lists conference and seminar fees only; owner decision D-068 (2026-09-18)
provisions.text: A job-related training course (an online course with a certificate that the supervisor or the project's PI asked for) is filed under 53251-CONFERENCE/SEMINAR/TRAINING EXPENSE, the one type whose name says training, with a needs_review flag: the manual lists conference registration and seminar fees as allowable and says nothing about training courses, so the type is our reading, to be confirmed

Funds for distribution to human subjects can be advanced through iBuy+ Expense; payments to research subjects are 55541-PAYMENTS TO SUBJECTS (on the OVPR list). Gift cards for subjects go through the Gift Card Order Form, not a line (NC-GIFT-CARDS); whether a subject payment other than gift cards is filed under 55541-PAYMENTS TO SUBJECTS was not verified — no situation yet

provisions.page: owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 13); owner decisions D-048, D-058 (2026-09-17) and D-067 (2026-09-18); https://ibuy.gwu.edu/expense-reporting-helpful-guidelines
provisions.text: An account on GW's OVPR list that this test account cannot select (52131, 52615, 53132, 53211, 55161, 55561, 58323, 58417, 58516, 58522, 58523, 58524, 58535, 58536, 58691) gets no line: the agent says the document is not filed in Concur, names the account by its code and name, and names the channel — never a nearby selectable type in its place

Where GW publishes no definition of the accounts that could take a line (52691 against 52441, 52721 against 53241 and 53251, 56311 against 55591), the defensible types are all accepted and the line carries a needs_review flag that the type is to be confirmed, in words tied to that line

A permit, licence or registration fee a lab pays for university business (the FAA registration of research drones) is 52441-PERMITS LICENSES & FEES — GW publishes no definition; not 58335-FEES/PERMITS, a capital-project type in our reading, nor 53111

provisions.page: p.19 (new manual p.19–20); owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 11); p.21, p.25 (new manual p.22, p.26)
provisions.text: Flowers or decorations for a university event bought on a foreign leg are 52613-NON US SPECIAL EVENTS/BUSINESS RELATIONS, the Foreign Travel Expense twin of 52612, recorded in the currency paid

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) App. A p.50 (item 36); App. B p.30; owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 8, by analogy)
provisions.text: An employer booth at a career fair paid personally is filed under 52641-RECRUITING EXPENSE with a needs_review flag: booth space is normally paid by the department on a P-Card or a Payment Request, and App. B puts payments to a service provider under the P-Card and invoice-processing policies

provisions.page: https://ibuy.gwu.edu/expense-reporting-helpful-guidelines (52691 on the OVPR list); Concur Add Expense dialog (52691 heads the Supplies section); experience
provisions.text: An office cost that is not a supply — a notary fee for a university document — is 52691-MISCELLANEOUS OFFICE EXPENSE; 52441 is accepted too, as GW defines neither (NC-TYPE-UNDEFINED)

provisions.page: https://ibuy.gwu.edu/expense-reporting-helpful-guidelines; https://compliance.gwu.edu/identification-and-treatment-unallowable-costs-sponsored-projects; App. A p.28 (new manual p.29); Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) App. A p.48 (item 14)
provisions.text: A fee paid to develop a new academic program (a program-design workshop) is 52721-PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITY — read as not a fundraising account, since GW lists 52722 but not 52721 as unallowable on sponsored projects; 53241 and 53251 are accepted too (NC-TYPE-UNDEFINED)

provisions.page: https://ibuy.gwu.edu/expense-reporting-helpful-guidelines (54541 on the OVPR list, 54111 not); https://ibuy.gwu.edu/facilities-and-mro-supplies; owner decision D-064 (2026-09-18)
provisions.text: Supplies that are neither office nor laboratory supplies — moving boxes and packing material for a lab move — are 54541-MISCELLANEOUS SUPPLIES, not 54111 or 54121; bought out of pocket they are filed without the preferred-channel notice, which D-064 keeps to subscriptions, cloud services, office supplies and dues

provisions.page: App. A p.28 (new manual p.29); Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.3, p.45–46; https://taxdepartment.gwu.edu/worker-classification; owner decision 2026-09-17 (no. 8, by analogy)
provisions.text: An employee who paid a contracted consultant's airfare files it under 55112-CONSULTANTS TRAVEL (53131 accepted) with a needs_review flag: GW pays a consultant's travel itself on a P-Card or on the consultant's invoice under the agreement; the consultant's own receipts are a non-employee reimbursement in Concur Invoice

provisions.page: https://business-services.gwu.edu/sites/g/files/zaxdzs6001/files/downloads/LTP_1920_8_Departmental%20Guidelines_Remediated.pdf; Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.18; owner decision D-016 (2026-09-14); experience
provisions.text: Promotional items bearing GW's marks are 55152-PUBLICITY & PROMOTION, made by a GW-licensed vendor after Licensing & Trademarks approved the artwork: the approval is attached to the line (our judgment), and without it the line is filed with a needs_review flag asking for it

55152-PUBLICITY & PROMOTION is on GW's list of costs unallowable on sponsored projects and 2 CFR 200.421 bars promotional items: on a federal award the line carries a needs_review flag to move it to an unrestricted account

Payments to research subjects made from a human-subjects cash advance are 55541-PAYMENTS TO SUBJECTS, filed once the subjects were paid, with the signed payment log; every advance must be applied to an expense report, and as this test account holds no advance the line carries a needs_review flag

Cash a researcher paid study participants from their own pocket is not filed in Concur although 55541 is selectable: GW's route is Advarra (Forte) Participant Payments, or a method the Finance Division approves before the study (that the cash cannot be claimed afterwards is our reading)

A meeting room rented for part of a day is 55591-BUILDING/ROOM/FACILITY RENTAL (SHORT TERM), not lodging or an event cost; GW sources hotel meeting and event space through Procurement (Hotel & Event Request), so a room an employee booked and paid is filed with a needs_review flag

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.4, p.46; https://finance.gwu.edu/departments; owner decision D-055 (2026-09-17)
provisions.text: A monthly desk or space membership is 56311-BUILDING/ROOM/FACILITY RENTAL OCCUPANCY (55591 accepted: GW defines neither); a licence for the use of space is a real-estate transaction for GW's Office of Real Estate that an employee does not sign, so the line carries a needs_review flag for each question

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.33–34; https://procurement.gwu.edu/media/2141 p.34 (§6.1.2)
provisions.text: Only individuals with a specific delegation of authority sign contracts that bind GW for goods, services, equipment or construction: a lease or a contractor's proposal an employee signed may not bind GW and the signer may become personally liable

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.3, p.46; https://procurement.gwu.edu/multi-function-device-suppliers; https://procurement.gwu.edu/media/2141 p.34 (§6.2)
provisions.text: A lease of office equipment is a contract P2P processes (52131-LEASE-OFFICE EQUIPMENT, which this account cannot select): new copiers come only from GW's two contracted multifunction-device suppliers, requested on the order placement form through Gatekeeper; a payment on a lease an employee signed is not filed in Concur (not 52195 or 52691)

Gifts, prizes and awards to employees — a recognition outing the chair approved as an On-the-Spot award — are 52615-EMPLOYEE SPECIAL ACTIVITY, which this account cannot select: not filed in Concur; University Payables pays or reimburses non-taxable awards through the Payment Request Form, and a missing expense type is asked of the iBuy Help Desk; not 52611, 52612 or 57121

Travel of a trainee appointed on a training grant is 53132-TRAINEE TRAVEL, which this account cannot select: not filed in Concur — the grant's program coordinator and the Research Support Team charge it to the training grant (our reading: GW publishes no trainee-travel procedure), or the iBuy Help Desk is asked to add the type; no ordinary 531xx type in its place

provisions.page: App. B p.31; https://procurement.gwu.edu/media/2141 p.8; https://procurement.gwu.edu/international-transactions; Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) App. A p.50 (item 31); https://taxdepartment.gwu.edu/worker-classification-and-international-engagement-request-form-exemptions
provisions.text: A foreign individual's unpaid invoice for a professional service (a translation) is 55161-NON-US PROFESSIONAL SERVICES, which this account cannot select: University Payables pays it — the payee registers as a supplier with form W-8BEN and the approved invoice is paid by EFT through a Payment Request, no purchase order; services of international individuals are never paid on a P-Card

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.5, p.34, p.40; https://procurement.gwu.edu/media/2141 p.8; p.23 (new manual p.24)
provisions.text: A service bought under a statement of work is a contract P2P places — a purchasing requisition with the SOW, a purchase order, the invoices to University Payables — account 55561-CONTRACT SERVICE-OTHER in our reading, which this account cannot select; an unsigned statement of work is not proof of payment and nothing is filed

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.16, p.33–34; https://procurement.gwu.edu/media/2141 p.34; App. B p.30
provisions.text: Construction or renovation work in a GW building is 58323-OTHER CONSTRUCTION CONTRACTS, which this account cannot select: FPCM (Facilities Planning, Construction and Management) manages it and administers the construction contracts with P2P; a deposit an employee paid is not filed (not 58327-FIXED EQUIPMENT)

Furniture, copiers and laboratory instruments of $5,000 or more a unit (shipping, handling and installation included) with a useful life over one year are capitalized — 58417, 58535, 58536, none of them selectable: bought through Procurement (a purchase order in EAS or iBuy+), capitalized and tagged by the Controller's Fixed Assets department; not filed in Concur, and no part of the invoice becomes a line

provisions.page: Contract Process Guide (Procurement, 2025-04-30) p.3, p.34; https://transportation.gwu.edu/fleet; https://controller.gwu.edu/capitalized-asset-management
provisions.text: A vehicle for GW is 58516-CAPITALIZED VEHICLES EXPENSE, which this account cannot select: P2P handles vehicle leasing and purchasing and Transportation and Logistics administers GW's vehicles (the shared motor pool); a deposit an employee paid on one is not filed

Parts of a fabrication — a unique instrument of more than $5,000 assembled from parts, some or all under $5,000 — are capital even when each part is under $5,000: 58522-GW OWNED CAPITALIZED FABRICATION EQUIPMENT, or 58523-NON-GW OWNED CAPITALIZED FABRICATION EQUIPMENT when title vests in the sponsor; neither is selectable — the parts are bought through Procurement and the Fixed Assets department records the fabrication

Equipment whose title vests in the Government under a federal cost-reimbursement contract (FAR 52.245-1) is not a GW asset: 58691-EQUIPMENT-NOT GWU in our reading (no GW page defines it), which this account cannot select — bought through Procurement on the contract and recorded as government property by the Fixed Assets department

provisions.page: Concur Add Expense dialog, Supplies section (EXPENSE_CATEGORIES.md §1.1, read 2026-09-15); owner decision D-065 (2026-09-18); experience
provisions.text: The Supplies section names the KIND of the goods — 54111 office, 54112 library, 54121 laboratory, 54131 linen, 54141 instructional, 54151 printing, 54161 athletic, 54531 photographic, 54541 miscellaneous: supplies of a named kind take that account, not the office type (54111) and not the residual one (54541, which is for supplies of no named kind — NC-MISC-SUPPLIES). Where the kind of the goods is itself arguable the defensible accounts are all accepted, with the type flag (NC-TYPE-UNDEFINED)

provisions.page: https://ibuy.gwu.edu/lab-supplies-equipment-0; https://compliance.gwu.edu/direct-charging-administrative-costs-associated-sponsored-projects; https://sponsoredprojects.gwu.edu/budget-cost-categories; Concur Add Expense dialog (54121 in the Supplies section)
provisions.text: Consumables of a laboratory — reagents, gloves, pipette tips, dry ice — are 54121-LABORATORY SUPPLIES. They are a DIRECT cost of the research, not one of the administrative costs GW's direct-charging page lists (subscriptions, computers, general office supplies, memberships, postage): on a federal award a laboratory-supply line needs no administrative-cost flag and no sponsor-approval question (NC-GRANT-ADMIN-COSTS does not reach it)

provisions.page: https://controller.gwu.edu/capitalized-asset-management; Concur Add Expense dialog, Equipment section; owner decision D-079 (2026-09-20)
provisions.text: Furniture and equipment under $5,000 a unit is not capitalized (NC-CAPITALIZED-5000): the Equipment section splits it in two — 52191-NON-CAPITALIZED INSTRUCTIONAL & LAB FURNITURE EQUIPMENT for what furnishes a laboratory or a classroom, 52195-OTHER NON-CAPITALIZED FURNITURE & EQUIPMENT for the rest of an office. A computer stays 52193 (NC-COMPUTER-GWIT); an office device is equipment, not a supply (54111) and not a miscellaneous office expense (52691)

GW asks departments to buy furniture, equipment and services to the university's standards, through Procurement and its contracted suppliers, and to consult P2P before departing from them: furniture an employee bought out of pocket is filed with a needs_review flag naming the standardization policy (the page does not say the purchase is void — the flag asks, it does not refuse)

provisions.page: Concur Add Expense dialog, Printing/Copying section; experience (GW's manual does not mention printing, copying or binding)
provisions.text: An outside shop's invoice for BINDING alone — no printing on it — is 55513-BINDING, the section's own type; 55511-NON-GW PRINTING/REPRODUCTION is printing and reproduction and 52661-OFFICE COPYING - NOT GWU is copying (NC-PRINTING covers an invoice that mixes them)

provisions.page: Concur Add Expense dialog, Books/Subscriptions section; experience
provisions.text: A library's SERVICE — document delivery, a copyright-cleared article, digitisation, an audiovisual service — is 52716-AUDIOVISUAL/LIBRARY SERVICES, next to 52221-SUBSCRIPTIONS/PERIODICALS and 52231-BOOKS in the same section: a service bought item by item is neither a subscription (nothing recurs) nor a book

provisions.page: https://transportation.gwu.edu/fleet; https://transportation.gwu.edu/fleet-rental; App. B p.30; Concur Add Expense dialog (54511 is the Vehicle Expense section's only type)
provisions.text: Fuel an employee paid for a GW FLEET vehicle is filed under 54511-FUEL-GASOLINE AND OIL, with a needs_review flag: Transportation and Logistics settles a fleet rental's final costs 'by an interdepartmental assessment via a journal entry' and publishes nothing about fuel, so whether the fill-up belongs in that charge is to be confirmed. App. B's unallowable fuel is the fuel of a PERSONAL car, which mileage already pays for (GT-GAS-PERSONAL); a rental car's fuel on a trip stays with the trip's ground transportation

Taxation of gifts, prizes and awards to employees: de minimis non-cash gifts up to $100; departments generally may not use the P-Card for awards

Fixed Asset Management Policy: fixed assets are bought on a PO in EAS or through iBuy+; a fabrication (a unique asset over $5,000 built from parts, some or all under $5,000) is reported to the Fixed Assets Department; government property defined
Transportation and Logistics: fleet — the assignment, use and replacement of university vehicles; a shared motor pool of vans and trucks

Transportation and Logistics: fleet rental — a unit reserves a vehicle in the Fleet Commander system; 'Payment for the final costs incurred during the rental period will be processed by an interdepartmental assessment via a journal entry'. The page says nothing about fuel or refuelling (read 2026-09-20)
